title: The modern saints, again
tomorrow: a saint for every day: too much, or exactly right?

cards: Nobody saves their boss in their phone as master. The word sounds like chains. So here's the odd detail.
Josephine Bakhita was kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold as a slave. Years later, free and living in Italy, she spoke of God with the local word for master: paron.
Why would a woman who'd escaped her masters call God one? Pope Benedict the Sixteenth told her story at the start of a letter on hope, and the answer is in it.

teach.h: THE SAME WORD, A DIFFERENT MASTER.
teach.b: Bakhita had known masters who beat her. Then, the pope writes, she came to know a completely different kind of master: the living God, who loved her. The word stayed the same.
The one behind it changed. That's the puzzle solved. For her, master wasn't a chain anymore.
It was the name of someone who'd set her free. She was baptized and became a sister, and the Church now calls her a saint.
She stands with others back on the climb. Óscar Romero, an archbishop in El Salvador who spoke up for the poor and was killed while celebrating Mass.
Maximilian Kolbe, a Polish friar who stepped forward in a Nazi camp to take the place of a man condemned to die. Teresa of Calcutta, who cared for the dying in the streets.
And Carlo Acutis, a teenager who loved computers and the Eucharist.
Here's the one to tell a friend: these saints had passports and newspapers, and some of them had email. The Letter to the Hebrews speaks of "so great a cloud of witnesses" around us.
The modern saints say that cloud never stopped growing.
Holiness didn't end with the old stories. It happened in camps and cities and bedrooms with a computer in them.

how: Catholics ask the saints to pray for them, much as they would ask a friend, and keep holy cards and feast days of recent saints alongside the ancient ones.

games.q: you're Bakhita. you were owned by cruel masters, and now you're free and baptized. which word do you use for God?
o: master: the same word, about someone completely different.
a brand-new word with no past attached to it.
no word at all; titles only remind you of chains.
games.why: she called God paron, master. Pope Benedict writes that she had come to know a totally different kind of master, one who loved her.

practice: Choose one of them: Bakhita, Romero, Kolbe, Teresa or Carlo. Say the name out loud, slowly, and remember one thing that saint did.
If you pray, you can add the words Catholics say with any saint's name, pray for us; if not, let the name and the story be enough.

wordCard.voice: The modern saints. People the Church calls holy who lived in a world a lot like ours.

orig.note: Venetian dialect, written in Latin letters: master, boss. the word Bakhita used for the living God.

carryVoice: Carry this: saints of our time, with passports and phones and the same God as the martyrs. Until tomorrow.
